'''Daniel Harlow''' is the [[Jerrold R. Zacharias]] Career Development Associate Professor of Physics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Daniel Harlow » MIT Physics |url=https://physics.mit.edu/faculty/daniel-harlow/ |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=MIT Physics |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Harlow was born in [[Cincinnati]] and grew up in [[Boston]] and [[Chicago]]. He received his B.A. from [[Columbia University]] in 2006 and his Ph.D. from [[Stanford University]] in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-12-27 |title=Newsmakers |url=https://www.college.columbia.edu/cct/issue/winter18/article/newsmakers |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=Columbia College Today |language=en}}</ref> Before joining MIT's faculty in July 2017, he was a postdoctoral fellow at [[Princeton University]] and [[Harvard University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=School of Science welcomes new faculty members |url=https://news.mit.edu/2017/mit-school-of-science-welcomes-new-faculty-members-1010 |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=MIT News {{!}} Massachusetts Institute of Technology |date=10 October 2017 |language=en}}</ref>

His research is focused on understanding black holes and cosmology, viewed through the lens of quantum field theory and quantum gravity.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Siegel |first=Ethan |title=Ask Ethan: What Does It Mean That Quantum Gravity Has No Symmetry? |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/startswithabang/2019/06/29/ask-ethan-what-does-it-mean-that-quantum-gravity-has-no-symmetry/ |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>

Harlow won the [[New Horizons in Physics Prize]] in 2019 for "fundamental insights about quantum information, quantum field theory, and gravity."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Speakers and Panelists {{!}} Breakthrough Prize Symposium |url=https://breakthroughprize.berkeley.edu/speakers#:~:text=Daniel%20Harlow%20received%20the%202019,of%20black%20holes%20and%20cosmology. |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=breakthroughprize.berkeley.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Breakthrough Prize – Fundamental Physics Breakthrough Prize Laureates – Daniel Harlow |url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/1/L3835 |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=breakthroughprize.org |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author1=Mike Wall |date=2018-10-17 |title=2019 Breakthrough Prize Honors Pulsar Discovery, 'Multi-Messenger Astronomy' and More |url=https://www.space.com/42168-breakthrough-prize-pulsars-multimessenger-astronomy.html |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=Space.com |language=en}}</ref> He was also named a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Research Fellow]] in 2019,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Four from MIT named 2019 Sloan Research Fellows |url=https://news.mit.edu/2019/four-from-mit-named-sloan-research-fellows-0221 |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=MIT News {{!}} Massachusetts Institute of Technology |date=21 February 2019 |language=en}}</ref> and in 2020, he was named a [[Packard Fellow]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Daniel Harlow awarded Packard Foundation Fellowship |url=https://news.mit.edu/2020/daniel-harlow-packard-foundation-fellowship-1020 |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=MIT News {{!}} Massachusetts Institute of Technology |date=20 October 2020 |language=en}}</ref>
